mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each partner and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or competent state registry of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (unless issued in EU/EEA or with a Luxembourg recognized notarial certification)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / lacuna certificate for any corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential and business address (utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy with apostille (for non-EU issuers); EU-origin documents rely on notarial certified copy only

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney granted to the Luxembourg incorporation agent / PFS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Partner granting authority, notarized in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, partners and controlling managers against (i) Luxembourg and EU consolidated sanctions lists, (ii) UN Security Council listings, (iii) FATF public statements, and (iv) domestic regulatory disqualification lists. PEPs are identified per EU AMLD standards, including family members and known close associates, as implemented by the Law of 12 November 2004. Although OFAC is not directly binding in Luxembourg, international correspondent banking and USD-denominated settlements impose an implicit contractual OFAC screening obligation on all target payment rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), electronic platform for the Register de Commerce et des Societes (RCS), accessible via lbr.lu / rcs.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be expressed in Latin script; non-Latin scripts require transliteration into French, German, or Luxembourgish. The partnership name must be immediately preceded or followed either by 'SCSp' or 'Societe en commandite speciale'. The name may be in any language provided it does not contravene public order. RCS filings are accepted in French or German; an English or other-language name must be accompanied by a certified translation into one of those languages.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS rejects the proposed name, the applicant may request the Registrar's written reasons and file an administrative appeal with the District Court of Luxembourg (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within 15 days of notification, alternatively resubmit a modified name within the same business day. If the refusal is maintained, an administrative act appeal may be lodged with the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) under the Law of 1 December 1978 on administrative procedure. All appeals must be accessed via Luxembourg counsel and require payment of the relevant court fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an industrial-grade manufacturing scope (compression molding of food-grade silicone), a pure virtual office without physical presence is not acceptable. The SCSp must maintain a Luxembourg registered office at the principal place of administration; outsourcing administrative and accounting functions to an authorized PFS satisfies the minimum substance if books and records are kept locally and strategic decisions are made by Luxembourg-domiciled managers. No manufacturing activity may be physically conducted at a virtual office address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 10% for a low-risk commercial operator, but likelihood materially increases to 25% if the tax administration or social security authorities question substance or if the SCSp claims treaty benefits or pass-through tax treatment.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the RCS fee schedule (Loi du 13 decembre 1993, as amended)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translations and apostilles for individual IDs, proof of address, and corporate certificates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for boutique law firms, EUR 250-400 per hour, flat fee for standard incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration, publication in the electronic Recueil des Societes (RESA), and related formalities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing and publication tariff (fixed fees)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC onboarding, UBO declaration filing, PEP and sanctions screening setup
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulatory fee and initial compliance database subscription (annualized pro-rata month)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended; specifically Articles 565-1 to 565-5 introducing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) by the Law of 12 July 2013.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), resident at 6, Avenue du Swing, L-4367 Belvaux, Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form C SCSp – Déclaration de création d'une société en commandite spéciale (RCS registration form) together with the contractual partnership agreement (contrat de société).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an SCSp; partners freely determine capital contributions in the partnership agreement. No escrow account is required by law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the SCSp is duly established pursuant to the partnership agreement dated [Date]; that the registered office of the SCSp is fixed at [Luxembourg address]; that [Name] is appointed as general partner (associé gérant) to legally bind the partnership; that [Name] is appointed as manager with exclusive power to open bank accounts and execute commercial agreements; and that annual financial records shall be prepared in accordance with Luxembourg commercial law. Further resolved that the initial capital, without statutory minimum, shall be subscribed in accordance with the partners' capital accounts, and the RCS filing be authorized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the SCSp Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partners directly; notarial deed optional (private writing sufficient unless any partner holds real estate in Luxembourg).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the contrast de société expressly qualifying as an SCSp under Article 565-1 et seq. Include the exact firm name, Luxembourg registered office address, corporate purpose (manufacturing and sale of silicone tactile sensory fidgets), identity and contribution of each partner, the general partner's management powers, and profit-sharing rules. Execute the agreement by all partners.
required_dossiers: Draft SCSp partnership agreement
Copy of valid passport or national ID of each partner
Proof of residential address of each partner
Declaration of ultimate beneficial owner(s) (UBO) for AML purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a name conflict, amend the partnership agreement by simple private act or notarial rectification and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Verification and Submission to the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the e-RCS online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform an online name availability check on the RCS database. File Form C (SCSp) through the e-RCS portal, attaching the executed partnership agreement, proof of any legal person general partner's authorisation, and payment of the registration fee.
required_dossiers: Form C SCSp (duly signed)
Executed partnership agreement
Identification documents of all partners and the general partner
If the general partner is a legal entity: articles of association and a board resolution appointing a representative
Criminal record extract for any individual manager with disciplinary powers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The RCS may issue a request for completion (advisory notice) requiring missing information; respond within one month via the e-RCS portal; any refusal is subject to appeal before the Luxembourg District Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Compulsory Publication in the Official Electronic Gazette (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Publication automatically arranged by the RCS in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA) of the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the RCS entry, the registry electronically transmits the filing details to RESA for publication. Verify the electronic extract through the RESA portal and retain a copy for contractual counterparties.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract (issued automatically)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or erroneous, submit a request to the RCS for correction; administrative rectification is processed within 5 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Tax Administration (Administration des contributions directes – ACD); Register, Estates and VAT Authority (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA – AEDT); Social Security Centre (Centre commun de la sécurité sociale – CCSS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp on the Luxembourg national business identification system (matricule) via Guichet.lu. Apply for a VAT number if the partnership will engage in taxable manufacturing activity. Register as a social security employer with the CCSS for any personnel.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate (extract)
SCSp partnership agreement
Identification of the general partner
Proof of registered office address
If employing staff: nationality and social identification documents of employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ACD or AEDT queries the registration, submit a corrective statement via MyGuichet; missing UBO declarations may be cured by filing an addendum with the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Bank Account and Corporate Housekeeping Implementation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed in Luxembourg (for payment rails SWIFT/TT and platform pay) and, if applicable, a professional registered office provider registered with the CSSF.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a business bank account in the name of the SCSp using the RCS extract and partnership agreement. The general partner must execute a bank opening resolution and provide KYC documents. Complete internal housekeeping: adopt a statutory corporate calendar, obtain an LEI code if engaging in financial transactions, and appoint an accountant.
required_dossiers: RCS registry extract
SCSp partnership agreement (certified copy)
Identification passports and proof of address of the general partner and beneficial owners
Bank-specific KYC forms and source of funds declaration
Registered office address proof if externally provided
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further due diligence, provide a copy of the beneficial ownership register or audited accounts; unresolved queries may be escalated to the bank's compliance committee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – the compression molding of food-grade silicone tactile sensory fidgets qualifies under ISIC 3240 as a small-scale novelty toy production; no sectoral manufacturing license is required under the Luxembourg Law of 24 July 1977 on the classification of dangerous establishments.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating permit; optional CE marking and Toy Safety Directive (2009/48/EC) compliance certificate required for market distribution.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration with the agence is required only if production exceeds 10 tonnes per year or generates hazardous waste; otherwise the activity is exempt from a full EIA report pursuant to the Law of 22 May 2008 on the environmental assessment of plans and programmes.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater parameters: pH 6.5–8.5, COD ≤ 125 mg/L, BOD ≤ 25 mg/L, no VOC emissions from silicone curing; waste silicone offcuts must be classified under the EU Waste Framework Directive (2008/98/EC) and disposed of via an approved recycler.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance must be obtained from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) confirming compliance with the Luxembourg fire protection code. A structural load certificate for the manufacturing space and an occupational health inspection by the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) are required to certify safe working conditions, emergency exits and machine safety (CE marked equipment).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for indirect taxes and VAT; central services and e-filing at www.guichet.lu / myguichet.lu, and the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) at www.lbrc.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Register the SCSp with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) to obtain a 13-digit registration number (matricule); file a direct tax registration notice with the ACD using Form 100 (and if applicable Form 100B) to obtain the fiscal number; file VAT registration Form 400 with the AEDT to obtain the VAT identification number (LU + 8 digits), which is mandatory for liable suppliers making taxable supplies above the exemption threshold, or voluntary where threshold not exceeded; foreign entities without a Luxembourg permanent establishment need no direct tax registration but must register for VAT for imports, distance sales, or domestic acquisitions above the thresholds, with possibility to appoint a fiscal representative when required by the AEDT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a domestic check-the-box classification regime. The SCSp is pass-through by default for income and net wealth tax purposes; no election is available to convert it into a corporate taxpayer. However, foreign investors may elect under their own tax classification rules (e.g., the U.S. check-the-box rules) to treat the SCSp as transparent or opaque; such classification mismatches are neutralised by Luxembourg's ATAD anti-hybrid rules, which operate automatically to deny deductions or reclassify income. For VAT, the SCSp remains an independent taxable person irrespective of direct-tax transparency and may voluntarily register below the threshold.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Luxembourg Value Added Tax (TVA / VAT) in conformity with the EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 of annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT) for Luxembourg-established taxable persons; non-established foreign suppliers must register from the first euro when they make taxable supplies in Luxembourg, unless covered by the Import One-Stop Shop (IOSS) or OSS schemes; intra-community distance sales are registrable once aggregate remote sales cross the EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, or e-invoicing stamping mandate is currently in force in Luxembourg. Taxable persons must issue invoices that satisfy the EU VAT invoicing rules and retain them for inspection; periodic VAT returns (Form 400) and European recapitulative statements (EC sales lists) are filed electronically via myguichet.lu/e-CDF. Structured e-invoicing (PEPPOL / e-Invoice EN 16931) may be used bilaterally, but no API reporting to the tax authority is required. Mandatory digital reporting is expected only upon implementation of the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) package.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods supplies qualify for 0% VAT where the silicone fidget toys are physically removed from Luxembourg and transported outside the European Union by the supplier or a carrier on the supplier's instructions, evidenced by a customs export declaration (SAD) accepted by the customs office of exit, together with transport documents and proof of delivery abroad. Services supplied to a non-EU business customer are outside the scope of VAT under the B2B place-of-supply rules; services closely connected to the exported goods (e.g., freight, handling, inspection) may be zero-rated if provided to a customer established outside the EU and directly linked to the export. The supplier must keep full commercial, transport, customs, and banking records to prove the linkage between the sale and the physical export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD EX) validated by Luxembourg customs or the EU exporting customs office
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill/CMR) naming the exporter and foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT credit evidence showing receipt of export proceeds from the foreign buyer
Transport instruction / carrier or 3PL letter of shipment
Foreign customs entry document of the importing country (where available)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities may re-open and reassess zero-rated export transactions within the statutory limitation period (generally 5 years, extended in cases of fraud or criminal proceedings). Any missing, false, or inconsistent export documentation causes the immediate reversal of the 0% treatment and makes the supply taxable at 17%, together with statutory interest and late-payment penalties. Deliberate or fraudulent export zero-rating attracts administrative fines up to 100% of the evaded VAT and criminal tax-fraud sanctions, including imprisonment for up to 5 years and fines, and the tax authorities may issue a retrospective recovery assessment for the entire amount together with a clawback of any input tax recovered. If export proceeds have not been repatriated within the 180-day foreign-exchange deadline, the relevant revenue may also be treated as non-export/taxable income and assessed accordingly.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting together with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking licensing, AML/CFT supervision, and payment institution oversight, and with the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance for sanctions and restrictive measures administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg, as a euro-area member, applies the EU free movement of capital under Articles 63–65 TFEU; the euro is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. There is no foreign-exchange control regime, no requirement of prior central-bank approval for inbound capital contributions, profit distribution, or repatriation, and no statutory restriction on transferring funds abroad. However, remittances must be executed through an authorised credit institution or payment institution and remain subject to CSSF anti-money-laundering checks, FATCA/CRS reporting, sanctions screening, and EU restrictive measures against targeted jurisdictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender, repatriation, or mandatory conversion requirement for export proceeds in Luxembourg; a Luxembourg exporter may lawfully hold export receivables in EUR or foreign currency, and may convert freely at market rates. The only administrative obligations are statistical reporting to the BCL within the balance-of-payments framework when an invoiced export transaction exceeds the applicable reporting threshold, and general documentation/transfer-pricing compliance for related-party sales.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational EUR Account
Operational EUR and Multi-Currency Treasury Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, Luxembourg (BCEE/Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR Account / Domestic Settlement Account
Segregated Treasury / Escrow Account for Private Partnerships

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium, only as a limited payment conduit. An offshore digital EMI cannot lawfully provide banking services in Luxembourg without a CSSF licence or an EU/EEA passport under the Payment Services Directive (PSD2), and no passport can be effective for a non-EEA EMI without a Luxembourg branch or authorised agent. EMIs may hold funds only as payment accounts, cannot grant credit, and are not suitable custodians for capital escrow; the SCSp should maintain a Tier-1 Luxembourg bank account as master treasury and use EMIs only for platform payouts with daily sweep to the master account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No CSSF statute or Luxembourg law requires in all cases that directors or beneficial owners appear physically at a bank branch; remote account opening is permitted if the bank completes enhanced video-identification and electronically signed mandates using an EIDAS-qualified electronic signature. In practice, for an SCSp controlled by a non-resident general partner, most Tier-1 banks require at least one online or physical interview of the responsible manager and the ultimate beneficial owner; a purely remote onboarding may be accepted only for low-risk EEA corporate groups.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered SCSp with multiple minority limited partners and no clear source of initial capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified partner register, signed subscription and capital call documents, bank reference from the funding partner's principal bank, source-of-wealth declarations, audited or management-account financial statements, and a reconciled funds-flow narrative supported by title documents and tax clearances where relevant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EEA ultimate beneficial owner with no verifiable commercial footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passport or national ID under EIDAS verification, proof of tax residence, CRS/FATCA self-certifications, local business registry extracts, professional references, source-of-income evidence such as salary records, dividends, or sale contracts, and a notarised declaration of source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Product scope mismatch between the silicone fidget supplier/manufacturer and the SCSp's stated ISIC 3240 activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Manufacturing and supply agreements, purchase orders, customs declarations, trade invoices, inspection certificates, food-grade silicone compliance certificates such as LFGB or FDA documentation, and, if platform-distributed, the marketplace seller agreement and settlement statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Heavy reliance on marketplace payout rails and third-party payment processors creating layering risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Online marketplace merchant agreement, payout reports, bank statements showing downstream sweeps, integrated ecommerce transaction records, and a documented treasury policy that all platform funds are settled to the Luxembourg bank account within agreed value dates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp's lack of legal personality and unclear appointment of the general partner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formalised limited partnership agreement, notarised or extract evidence of the general partner's corporate authorisation, power of attorney/resolution appointing the gérant, the LEI certificate, and the current ordinary representation disclosure provided to the bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or working-capital injections must be wired by SWIFT MT103 or equivalent with the Luxembourg beneficiary account stated for LU_SCSP and the final credit made to the IBAN of the Tier-1 bank; the remitter must insert the BCL balance-of-payments purpose code corresponding to a direct investment in a Luxembourg partnership, generally mapped to the EU BoP class for financial account / direct investment equity, in SWIFT fields 50K and 70, and should quote the LEI of the SCSp and the bank's client reference. The bank will verify that the instruction is sanction-compliant, that the remitter is matched to the filed UBO declaration, and that the purpose code is consistent with a capital contribution; a copy of the capital call and signed subscription letter should be pre-delivered to the bank so funds can be credited to the capital escrow account without restriction. Any transaction above the BCL's statistical-reporting threshold may require balance-of-payments reporting, but it does not constitute an authorisation or exchange-control requirement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments for purchased silicone raw materials, packaging, and logistics should be settled by: (i) bank wire via SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments or platform disbursements; (ii) SWIFT MT700/MT710 documentary letters of credit for bulk manufacturing batches where the supplier requires bank-guaranteed settlement; or (iii) documentary collection under documents against payment or documents against acceptance for low-risk recurring suppliers. Each disbursement must include the correct EU BoP goods or services purpose code, export or import invoice reference, customs valuation where relevant, and must pass the bank's sanctions, PEP, and OFAC-style screening. The treasury must maintain a mirror ledger of commercial contracts to ensure each payment has a defined trade cycle, avoiding fragmented third-party payments that trigger AML alerts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX spot contracts with Luxembourg authorised credit institutions for immediate settlement of EUR/USD and EUR/CNY trade exposure.

Outright deliverable FX forwards, standard and rolling, under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or third-party credit support annex, limited to committed foreign-currency payables and receivables with documented trade underlying.
FX swaps transacted at market points for managing temporary euro liquidity against USD receipts prior to conversion.
Cross-currency swaps used solely to fix the financing leg of longer-term supplier credit or capital expenditure, subject to EMIR clearing and margin rules.
European-style non-leveraged FX options for protecting against adverse exchange-rate movement on expected but not yet contracted cash flows.

Non-deliverable forwards for exotic or illiquid currencies only where there is demonstrable regulatory restriction preventing physical delivery, with documented hedge rationale and, if transacted with a non-EEA counterparty, enhanced EMIR/EWRA collateral treatment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register, including management report and auditor opinion where applicable (mandatory where the SCSp has a corporate general partner; otherwise generally exempt from publication)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS Luxembourg)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the end of the financial year; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 31 July of the following year; judicial extension possible before the competent court
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a reminder, then a court order with coercive astreinte of up to EUR 250 per day of delay; criminal fines of up to EUR 25,000 may be imposed; persistent default can lead to application for administrative deregistration of the entity and personal exposure of the general partner

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership data in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March covering the prior calendar year; any change in shareholding, transfer of partnership interests, or change in ultimate ownership must be notified within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm or update UBO information, or submission of false data, exposes the entity and the responsible general partner to criminal fines from EUR 500 up to EUR 1,250,000 for intentional violations; the RBE may also impose forced filing, access restrictions, and publication of sanctions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual direct tax declaration (corporate income tax return and net wealth tax return) only where the SCSp has elected corporate taxation under Article 175 LIR; if fiscally transparent, no entity-level direct tax return is due and partners report separately
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May of the year following the tax year; automatically extended to 31 July where the return is prepared by an approved tax adviser
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest accrues at the Luxembourg statutory default rate; administrative fines up to EUR 2,500 per late or incorrect return apply; the ACD may assess tax ex officio on an estimated basis and impose criminal penalties for evasive conduct

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A compulsory statutory audit by an approved réviseur d'entreprises is triggered where the SCSp exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds at the year-end: (i) balance sheet total of EUR 4.4 million, (ii) net turnover of EUR 8.8 million, (iii) average workforce of 50 employees. Mandatory audit may also arise from the partnership agreement, financial institutions, or CSSF rules if the SCSp is used as an investment vehicle.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Lux GAAP) as set out in the Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial and companies register and annual accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU may be applied where permitted; statutory tax computations follow the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR) basis.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must validate through the RBE online portal by 31 March each calendar year that the beneficial owner information on file remains accurate. Any transfer of partnership interest, change in control chain, or variation in shareholding percentages must be reported within 30 days. A look-through analysis is required for any corporate partner; where no natural-person beneficial owner can be identified, the senior managing general partner must be declared.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,600 – USD 5,500 per annum, typically covering Luxembourg registered office supply, domiciliation services, RCS/RBE filing assistance, and corporate secretarial support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,800 – USD 16,500 per annum for a full Lux GAAP statutory audit; USD 2,500 – USD 7,000 for a review-only or compilation assignment when no statutory audit is required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and solidarity surcharge; base CIT progressive: 15% on first €175,000, 31.5% on excess)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption (100% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains); IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income); notional interest deduction; investment tax credit; SCSp is tax-transparent unless opted into corporate taxation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 510 (partnership income tax return) filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 31 May of the following fiscal year; extensions up to 6 months available upon request

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the partnership (name, address, RCS number)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Luxembourg tax identification number and details of the tax representative if applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period start and end dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure alignment with the partnership's fiscal year; non-resident partners must report their share of income in their own jurisdiction

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable income (before allocation to partners)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute income according to Luxembourg GAAP and tax adjustments; non-resident partners are taxed on their distributive share

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of income to each partner (name, address, tax ID, share percentage)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List all partners, including non-residents; provide their tax residency and treaty status for withholding tax purposes

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and exemptions claimed (e.g., participation exemption, IP box)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach supporting documentation; non-resident partners must ensure eligibility under domestic law and tax treaties

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: €10 to €2,500 per month of delay; late payment interest: 0.6% per month on unpaid tax, capped at 10% of the tax due; additional penalties for gross negligence or fraud

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (statutory rate for dividends paid by a Luxembourg company; SCSp is tax-transparent, so distributions to partners are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax unless the partnership has opted for corporate taxation)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding tax under a double tax treaty, the beneficial owner must submit a tax residency certificate (TRC) from their home jurisdiction and complete Form 22 (application for reduced withholding tax) to the Luxembourg tax authority (ACD). The procedure requires prior approval for reduced rates; for EU residents, the EU Interest & Royalties Directive may apply with a simplified process.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 15%; treaty rates typically 0-10%; EU Interest & Royalties Directive: 0% if conditions met. Interest: statutory 15%; treaty rates typically 0-10%; EU Interest & Royalties Directive: 0% if conditions met.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if related-party transactions exceed €1,000,000; Master File required if group consolidated turnover exceeds €50,000,000
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as per EU ATAD and BEPS; SCSp is a partnership and generally not subject to corporate ESR, but must demonstrate real economic activity (office, staff, decision-making) to avoid being classified as a shell company or for tax residency purposes. The Luxembourg tax authority may challenge artificial arrangements lacking substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income, false deductions, or concealment of assets in the SCSp
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to €250,000 or 100% of evaded tax; criminal prosecution; additional penalties up to 200% of tax due
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managing partners may be held personally liable for civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 5 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp has no physical presence, no employees, no real decision-making, and is used solely for tax avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax treaty benefits; reclassification as a taxable entity; retroactive tax assessments; fines up to €50,000
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid taxes and penalties; potential criminal charges for aiding tax evasion

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence, reporting suspicious transactions, or maintaining proper records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €1,000,000; criminal sanctions for money laundering; freezing of assets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face personal fines, imprisonment up to 5 years, and disqualification from serving as directors

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain transfer pricing documentation or applying non-arm's length pricing in related-party transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income; penalties up to 10% of the adjustment; interest on underpaid tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for penalties if they knowingly approved non-compliant pricing; criminal charges for tax fraud in severe cases
